label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
read: RC2 30-page edition, draft PDF, 32 pages, built from dev at 5bde59a3 with the publisher's command (a local copy of the figures list for chapter 1's new Figure line)
first_impression: A handsome dark cover with six little characters, then a book that is mostly airy and friendly, until ten dashed 'Figure to come' boxes make the back half feel unfinished.

pages.what_i_see: Dark cover, strong title, six colour-coded cast cards with one-line moods, rainbow corner. Clear and inviting; only six of nine agents shown, which is fine for a cover.
Title page: title top-left, author and subtitle, then a lot of white. Plain, a little bare, but it breathes.
Contents page: six chapter names in a tiny block at the top, no page numbers, the rest of the page empty. Reads as near-empty and a contents list with no numbers is hard to use.

Chapter opens well: red bar, cast bar, narrator head, then the A-to-B 'slide versus a loop' drawing. But the new player 'Figure to come' dashed box starts at the foot and is split across the page break; the talk's player UI is still not shown.

Top of the page carries the tail of the split placeholder (a stray file path in small type), so a promised picture is just text. Rest breathes well: quote, rule, closing note. Narrator head repeats on every paragraph run, fine.

Right half of the loop drawing (circle of three arrows with tiny factory inside) sits at the top, separated from its left half on page 4 by a full page, so the 'half and half' idea is lost. Tiny agents inside the circle are too small to read. Body text below is comfortable.

Cast cards grid runs off the right margin (the right-hand cards are clipped), caption beneath is long and dense. Page then packs a words box, a 'Do this now', and the start of 'Where this came from' to the foot. The busiest page so far.
Five lines of 'Where this came from' spill over, then a nearly empty page. A near-empty page caused by a widow of a source note.

Chapter 2 opens cleanly. Two words boxes, how-to-read note, dev and conductor lines. Speaker heads show mood in italics; dev's two lines share one head. Reads well and the cheeky tone lands. Page is full but not crowded.

Ruv-sgit's lines and the narrator head sit jammed together; the four lit cast cards then run flush to the right edge with the greyed row clipped at the margin, and a long caption and source note crowd the foot. Cards repeat what the text just said.

The Wardley map is a dashed 'Figure to come' box at the top, though the text says 'Look at the bottom row first'. The key picture for the chapter is absent. Words box and clock section are comfortable.

The five-step wake dial with each agent at its minute is the best picture in the book: it shows the clock and the loop at once. Text below starts a new section at the foot with a continued run, acceptable.
The first-wake card with outcome 'partial' next to a big 162 is clear and helpful. Cast bar strip at four in the morning is small but legible. Slight crowding between card, record line and caption.

Short 'Do this now' and source note, then three quarters of empty page. The 'Do this now' instruction butts up against the narrator line with no space, an italic block running straight off a heading-like head.
Bar chart of wakes by hour with the 5-or-6-an-hour gap shaded is a strong picture and proves the nine-hours-alone claim. Plenty of room.
Two-panel reviewer/researcher card supports the dispute well. The speaker run is followable; researcher and reviewer alternate with heads and moods. Page is full but readable.
Three 'sent back' cards are helpful but small, the middle card is offset lower, and text inside is tiny. Speaker heads here stack tightly (the ruv-sgit and narrator heads nearly touch).
Afternoon-loop timeline is clean and useful, then a dashed 'Figure to come' box for the map of the day sits mid-page between the narrator text and the source note. Placeholder printed as text.
Relayed-word diagram (arrow blocked by a wall, question going straight to the editor) is simple and works. Good space around it.
Two lines of 'Do this now' carried over then a source paragraph and an empty page. Near-empty.
Last-ten-minutes dot timeline is clear. A touch dense at the top with its long caption, but the page holds together. Conductor lines readable.

HOLD file inside the greyed clock ring, with the 82 seconds card beside it. The big number is vivid; the ring with tiny greyed agents does little. A subhead 'Why stop then' sits near the foot with only one line under it.

Dashed 'Figure to come' box for three speech cards, then the interview strip, which runs off the right margin (last card clipped). Heading 'What did not work: the interview' appears right after the placeholder, a lot happening.

Densest page of text: several speaker runs, a long closing narrator paragraph and a grid of five 'did not work' cards that fit snugly with caption and source note. Cards help but add to the crowding; foot is clear.
Empty-chair strip again runs to the right edge, then text, 'Do this now', and the start of 'Where this came from' squeezed to the foot, splitting the source note onto the next page.
Four lines of source note on an otherwise blank page, a widow from the previous page.
Chapter 5 opens with a dashed placeholder for nine cast cards turning into files, which the sentence above describes. Then a long run of cast lines, each with its own head and mood. Readable.
Second placeholder (this book's team as cast cards) mid-page. Followed by two scenes in dense paragraphs; the page is full to the foot.
Two further 'Figure to come' boxes on one page (two cards from this book's record; three small factories joined in the middle). Together they make the page look unfinished.
A 'Map to come' box at the top, then five numbered steps in boxes. The steps are the most useful thing in the book for me and are well laid out, but the boxes sit tight to each other.
Another placeholder for the five steps as a path. Short 'Do this now', 'Zoom in', and a source note; comfortable spacing, space left at foot.
Series page with one paragraph and source note, rest blank. Fine as a back page but its narrator head sits above a long heading-less block.

pictures_that_work: 12: the five-step wake dial with each agent's minute
15: the hours bar chart showing nine hours of the factory's own clock
13: the first-wake card with the big 162
19: the relayed word stopped at the door, question to the editor
18: the afternoon-loop timeline of asks and returns
30: the five numbered steps panel (a layout rather than a picture, but the page I would pin up)
pictures_missing: 4-5: the talk's player UI (countdown, step controls, notes) that chapter 1 describes; placeholder splits across two pages
11: the Wardley map the text says to look at 'first'
18: the map of the day, who was on stage when
23: three speech cards of the editor's three accounts of why he stopped
27: nine cast cards turning into folders and files
28: this book's team as cast cards
29: two cards from this book's record (refusal and usage limit)
29: three people each with a small factory joined by one brief, board and hold
30: the map of one project's parts becoming the next one's
31: the five steps as a path with the 'do this now' cards
too_tight: 7: cast cards clipped at the right margin, long caption and notes
10: four-card row clipped at right edge, narrator and ruv-sgit heads jammed
17: speaker heads stacked with almost no gap
23: interview strip runs off the right margin
24: heaviest page, many speaker runs plus the card grid
25: strip clipped at the right, source note split across to page 26
14: 'Do this now' instruction butts straight against its narrator line
8, 20, 26 and 32 are the opposite problem: near-empty pages carrying only a source note
speakers_note: One head per run works, and the italic moods in brackets are the cheeky part I liked: 'unbudging', 'sheepish', 'proud, the fussy one'. Narrator against cast is clear by head. Where heads stack tightly (pages 10 and 17) it is a little harder to tell a run has changed. A new reader could not tell who 'ruv-sgit' is on first mention except from the cover.
words_on_this_page_boxes: They help. The pale blue boxes (pages 7, 9, 11, 21, 27) explain agent, repository, hold, wake and session just where the word first bites, and they are what lets a newsroom writer who is not an engineer keep going. They are visually distinct from the story and never crowd it. Page 9 has three close together; spread them.
top_three_fixes: Replace the ten dashed 'Figure to come' boxes with the real pictures, starting with the player UI on page 4 and the Wardley map on page 11; a dashed box reads as unfinished.
Stop the wide card rows and strips from running past the right margin (pages 7, 10, 23, 25) and give heads a little more space where speakers alternate fast (10, 17).
Pull the source notes that spill onto a nearly blank page (8, 20, 26) back onto the previous page or give them a short end-of-chapter page layout, and add page numbers to the contents on page 3.
notes: As a newsroom builder what I took away: one editor who signs, one page of rules, a hold, a board and a clear 'Do this now' at each chapter end. Page 30 gives me the five steps. The book reads better than it looks while the placeholders remain.
